must_ask_hmp: Current SF rental rate card (weekly and monthly) per model incl. deposit amount, insurance add-on, and rent-to-own schedule - the public page hides prices in images.
Battery subscription / swap plan pricing and terms (per-swap vs monthly, which models, swap-station count and throughput).
Actual fleet composition on rent (~100 vehicles) by model, and the ~300 battery subscribers by battery type (48V 24Ah e-bike packs vs 74V 45Ah moped packs).
Date the SF shop opened at 261 6th St and any prior locations (public evidence only supports 'founded 2022').
Dealer cost / landed cost per model vs the public MSRP (needed for unit economics; public sites only show retail and sale prices, which differ between hmpbikes.com and 415ebike.com).
Repair/parts revenue and warranty-claim rates, rental utilisation, theft/loss frequency (public page only shows the $150 / $500 / $25-per-month fee structure).
Which SKUs are intended for LA (Class 2 Inno/Liva vs M1-licensed FLASH/MK.II) and whether the 'HMP Bikes vs 415 eBikes' brand split will be replicated in LA.
surprises: Gazetteer SF (2026-04-02) reports 'over 600 e-mopeds in SF; targeting 1,000 by year-end', while the CONTEXT states >1,000 vehicles sold - reconcilable if the company figure is cumulative across all vehicle types or post-dates April, but the two should be reconciled with HMP.

HMP is headquartered in Davis, CA (440 F St; Gazetteer + Yelp + 'free local pickup in Davis and San Francisco') - 415 eBikes is described as HMP's SoMa 'dealership' / 'partner', not the parent; the LA hub would be a second retail outpost of a Davis brand.
The live SF storefront domain is 415ebike.com (singular); 415ebikes.com returned HTTP 503.

FLASH pricing differs by source: hmpbikes.com shows $4,999 sale / $5,499 regular, while July 2026 press quotes a $4,799 (single battery, no onboard charger) to $5,999 (dual battery + charger) ladder - configuration-dependent, so a single 'FLASH MSRP' default is ambiguous.
INNO-A Pro is $2,599 on hmpbikes.com but $2,699 on 415ebike.com (both 'sale' vs $2,799 regular).

FLASH and Lightning MK.II are DOT-registered motorcycles requiring an M1 licence - only the Inno/Liva Class 2 e-bikes and (likely) the Lightning 3000 mopeds fit the 'no license' courier positioning; the SF courier fleet described in press is Class 2 Inno-based, not FLASH/MK.II.
Battery-swap stations were slated to launch June 2026 (first at 415 eBikes) - so the ~300 battery subscribers in CONTEXT may be a very new product line with short operating history.
SWFT MAXX (named in CONTEXT) does not appear on either storefront's visible lineup.
